thread:
Noah: hi team, Noah here — on day 3. Building runtime from source on Ubuntu (WSL2). configure/make fail with: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory. I can run CUDA samples on Windows but not in the distro. any quick fixes?

Aisha: welcome! :wave: check `nvidia-smi` inside WSL first. If it errors, you probably need the Windows WSL-capable NVIDIA driver installed and then a `wsl --shutdown` + restart.

Noah: `nvidia-smi` was missing. Installed the WSL driver, restarted WSL. Now `nvidia-smi` works and `find / -name libcuda.so*` returns `/usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so.1`. but ldconfig -p doesn't list it and link still fails.

Sam: add the driver path to the dynamic linker: create `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/nvidia-wsl.conf` with `/usr/lib/wsl/lib` and run `sudo ldconfig`. Alternatively symlink the lib into `/usr/local/cuda/lib64`.

Noah: did the ld.so conf, ldconfig shows libcuda. build got past missing lib but now linker complains about undefined referencing `cuGetProcAddress`.

Aisha: that symbol is from newer driver APIs. Confirm the lib exports it: `readelf -s /usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so.1 | grep cuGetProcAddress`. If present, try moving `-lcuda` after other CUDA libs in your link command or wrap with `--start-group`/`--end-group`. Link order matters.

Noah: readelf shows the symbol present. Reordering libs fixed it. One more issue: docker test containers can't access /dev/nvidiactl — permission denied.

Sam: enable Docker Desktop WSL integration and install `nvidia-container-toolkit` in the distro. Use `--gpus all` when running. Also ensure your user is in `video` group so device nodes are accessible.

infra-bot: tip: add a short onboarding snippet to eng-runtime README about WSL driver, ld.so.conf, and docker GPU steps.

Noah: thanks everyone — build and container tests green now. I'll add the README note with the exact commands. :raised_hands:
